entries.claim: The pinned digital 51-word reading is a derived collation aid, not the controlling edition. It agrees with most of the body but omits eiusdem in the conclusion; the apparatus records that substantive omission and accidental variants.

locator.section: Feria II post dominicam I Passionis, Postcommunio (Sacramenti tui); seventeen-word conclusion prefix

entries.claim: The accented seventeen-word prefix through Deus supports tuum: Qui, no comma after Christum, and Sancti, Deus. It ends with a full stop here and does not print per omnia saecula saeculorum or Amen at this locus.
The unaccented ordinary full Father-directed formula supplies 21 words followed by Amen. The proper cue and RG 115 e add eiusdem; this locus alone does not establish the variant.

locator.section: Ordo Missae terminal chant and response

entries.claim: This chant prints Per omnia saecula saeculorum and Amen. The joined prose conclusion uses lower-case per after Deus; this is a declared presentation seam, not a continuous print locus for this prayer.

This page identifies and prints the 29-word proper body and its short Per Dominum ... in unitate eiusdem conclusion. It does not print the expanded conclusion continuously; the declared shared uses supply that expansion.

locator.section: RG 480–481, 511 d/i, 513–514; Ordo Missae rubric and chant formula after the secrets

entries.claim: The final secret has an audible Per omnia saecula saeculorum followed by the response Amen. Collects and postcommunions are priestly orations with a separate response. These rules determine the modeled boundaries, not the completeness of a date-specific commemoration inventory.

RG 115 e requires in unitate eiusdem Spiritus Sancti when the Holy Spirit is mentioned. This prayer explicitly mentions Spiritus Sancti in its body and prints the eiusdem short cue; preserve that variant. RG 116 preserves peculiar proper conclusions.
